newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan calls Jerusalem bombing "abominable".
newsitem.headline: Annan calls Jerusalem bombing "abominable".

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan called Wednesday's bombing of a Jerusalem market "abominable and unfortunate," especially at a time when efforts were being made to get Middle East peace talks back on track.
"And I appeal to all involved to avoid the use of bombs and violence and really get back to the negotiating table," he said.
In remarks to Cable News Network (CNN), Annan was reacting to an attack by two Arab suicide bombers on West Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda market that killed 13 people and wounded more than 150.
"I think it is abominable and unfortunate, particularly at a time when all efforts are being made to get the peace talks back on track," the U.N. chief said.

He recalled telling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a telephone conversation on Monday he was encouraged that he had suspended construction of a controversial housing project in an Arab neighbourhood in East Jerusalem.
"And so I am disappointed that at a crucial time when we were just on the verge of getting the talks back on track that this should happen," Annan said.
